text:
maria: Heads up — after the kernel-selector rollout last night, Qwen2.5 p99 latency spiked ~18% for requests with mixed CJK + latin. Perf job attached (quick profile).

jon: saw that in dashboards. Tokenization-heavy tails only show up on multi-ling payloads. Single-lang en-only looks fine.

perf-bot: nightly-perf-job/report: qwen2p5-mainline - p50: 42ms -> 44ms, p95: 110ms -> 115ms, p99: 210ms -> 248ms, kv cache miss rate: 2.1% -> 9.7%

siva: interesting — KV cache miss rate jump points to either cache key formation or invalidation. Any chance tokenizer output shape changed and we started sharding/kvs by subtoken_count vs token_count?

anna: I pushed the kernel selector tweak: heuristic now uses `tokens_estimate = max(1, int(seq_len / avg_subtoken_ratio))` rather than the previous `subtoken_count` estimate. That was to reduce kernel churn for long synthetic sequences.

maria: here's the slice from the profiler where the latency appears:
```
# per-request timeline (example)
recv -> tokenize: 6ms
tokenize -> kernel-select: 1ms
kernel-launch -> kv-lookup: 2ms
kv-lookup -> kv-miss-path: 110ms
kv-miss -> first-token-gen: 80ms
```
The kv-miss path time is huge for these multi-ling examples.

jon: can you paste a raw tokenizer output for a failing example? I want to see subtoken boundaries.

maria: sample input: "今天 we shipped the change"
maria: tokenizer output (subtokens): ["今天", "Ġwe", "Ġshi", "pped", "Ġthe", "Ġchange"]

anna: ah — our split produced a multi-token for the CJK word (single token) vs latin splits where we rely on Ġ markers. If the kernel selector is grouping by estimated tokens, KV key might be constructed using token offsets that mismatch existing cache keys built from actual subtoken indices.

siva: that mismatch could cause us to generate a different KV namespace per request, triggering cache misses even though the underlying model state would have matched. Two immediate theories: 1) cache key includes `token_index_bucket` derived from tokens_estimate (new), 2) ALiBi/RoPE scaling variant changed the head->kv mapping and we now choose different kernel layout which uses different cache key prefix.

jon: I grepped the cache key code — prefix is `kvcache:v1:{model}:{variant}:{kv_bucket}` where `kv_bucket` = `floor(prefix_len / bucket_size)` and bucket_size is computed from kernel heuristic. So changing the heuristic will change bucket_size.

maria: reproduce steps I ran:
```bash
# reproduce failing pattern
python perf_runner.py --model qwen2p5 --input "今天 we shipped the change" --profile --repeat 50
# observe cache miss ratio in logs
grep -E "kvcache.*miss" perf_logs.txt | wc -l
```
I can share perf_logs.txt.

perf-bot: trace snippet: kvcache miss for request_id=... reason=kv_bucket_mismatch (expected bucket 42, computed 57)

anna: OK — this is a legitimate regression introduced by the selector heuristic changing bucket_size. The kernel choice and bucket computation should be orthogonal to tokenizer decisions. Noted my mistake: I normalized by estimated tokens to reduce kernel switching, but didn't lock kvcache bucketization to actual tokenizer output.

siva: short-term mitigation: revert kernel-selector heuristic and roll forward a patch that derives bucket_size from `subtoken_count` (the tokenizer's output length) or, better, compute bucket from canonicalized `cache_index` emitted by tokenizer. That will avoid heuristic-induced namespace churn.

jon: agree. Also add a regression test: randomized mixed-ling inputs and assert kvcache namespace stability across selector config toggles.

maria: +1. For the revert, I'm going to open a quick PR and run the smoke job.

anna: I'll pair on the PR and add the tokenizer->kvcache integration test. Also will add a note in changelog and telemetry to emit `kvcache_bucket_v2` vs `v1` when heuristics change so we can spot these churns early.

infra-bot: deploy: rollback-kernel-selector v1.2 -> v1.1 triggered by maria at 2709876580 :robot_face:

jon: after rollback, initial perf_job shows p99 back down to 222ms (still slightly higher than before, but KV miss rate drops to 2.6%). Need a full-sized overnight run.

maria: action items: 1) revert landed (maria+anna) 2) add deterministic kvcache key path (anna) 3) regression suite for mixed-ling tokenizer + selector toggles (jon) 4) perf run overnight and alert if kv miss > 4% (siva)

siva: note for follow-up design doc — consider decoupling kernel_bucket from cache namespace entirely; cache should be stable across kernel/kind heuristics, otherwise we'll keep eating misses when we iterate on runtime.

maria: thanks team. I'll update the incident ticket with this thread and close after overnight looks green. :white_check_mark:
